## No operator decision needed — the convention is already established, and there is a SIBLING

This was queued as "needs a notification target from the operator". It does not: the target is
already the repo-wide convention, and this alarm is simply the odd one out.

Audited every `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` in `infra/terraform/`:

    HAS-ACTIONS  g2p_dispatch_errors             monitoring_1fa8.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  review_bot_merge_change_errors  monitoring_88ab.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  deploy_errors                   monitoring_autodeploy.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  review_interrupts               monitoring_autodeploy.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  root_disk_pressure              monitoring_autodeploy.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  bedrock_invoke_client_errors    monitoring_eb6e.tf
    NO-ACTIONS   voter_errors                    monitoring_s4b.tf     <-- this ticket
    NO-ACTIONS   replication_errors              monitoring_s5.tf      <-- SIBLING, unreported
    HAS-ACTIONS  mirror_out_of_sync              monitoring_ws7.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  gerrit_gate_down                monitoring.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  ec2_system_check                monitoring.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  ec2_instance_check              monitoring.tf
    HAS-ACTIONS  gerrit_data_disk_high           monitoring.tf

Eleven of thirteen set `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` AND `ok_actions` to the same
shared topic. Two do not. So the fix is to follow the existing pattern, not to choose a target.

`monitoring_1fa8.tf:38` even documents the intent in a comment: it says it "mirrors S4b's
voter_errors" structurally — while S4b is precisely the one missing the actions it is supposedly
being mirrored from.

## The sibling

`replication_errors` (`monitoring_s5.tf:30`) has the identical defect and no ticket. Same
consequence: the alarm transitions OK -> ALARM and notifies nobody. It should be fixed in the
same change rather than rediscovered later — this is the fourth time in one session that fixing
one instance of a defect surfaced more of the same (34c2 -> four guards, 7e90 -> eleven CI steps,
c5b3 -> two imports, and now this).

## Caveat that must not be lost

Landing terraform is NOT applying it. Bug 1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38 records that Terraform drift never
gates a Gerrit change, so un-applied infra can land and read as done. Whoever takes this must say
explicitly whether the change has been APPLIED, or the alarm still notifies nobody while the
ticket reads closed.
